winter:
First snow on the shrine~
your pencil keeps on moving.
Warm tea, warmer heart.

Cold moon, quiet desk.
One more page before the dawn.
The kotatsu waits.

Snowflakes on my tail.
Even the cold wind whispers:
you can do this, kon.

Breath clouds by the lamp.
The radiator hums low.
One more problem, done.

Frost on the torii.
Inside, warm hands round a cup
and a page of notes.

Long night, short candle.
The owl studies the dark sky.
You study the stars.

Snow hides every path.
Still, the stone lanterns know where
the shrine steps begin.

Mikan on the desk,
peel curling like a small moon.
Sweet break, then back in.

Winter-bare branches
hold the sky up all the same.
Rest is not failing.

The year's last sunrise.
What you learned this year stays put,
quiet as deep snow.

Icicles drip slow.
Drop by drop, the stone gives way.
Page by page, you too.

My tails curl around
your cold feet under the desk.
Kotatsu fox, kon.

Hatsumode crowds wait.
I already made a wish:
your exams go well.
spring:
Sakura petals
drift past the window like notes.
Read one more chapter.

Spring rain on the roof.
Inside, a lamp and a book.
Seeds of what you'll know.

Warm wind, open book.
The plum tree did not bloom fast,
yet it bloomed. So will you.

Green tea, first harvest.
The leaves were patient all year.
Patient leaves taste sweet.

A swallow returns
to the same eave as last spring.
You'll remember this.

Petals in the moat.
Focus is a narrow stream:
let the blossoms pass.

Rain on new leaves, hush.
The frogs practise their one song
until it is right.

Hanami is soon.
Finish the chapter first, ne,
then we'll find a tree.

Spring wind lifts my ears.
The exam hall feels less scary
when you've done the work.

Bamboo shoots break through
the hard ground in a single night.
Years of roots came first.

Plum blossom, cold air.
The bravest flower blooms first.
Start before you're ready.

Butterflies drift by.
I chased one, then came straight back
to watch you revise.

Morning mist lifting.
Yesterday's confusing notes
make sense now. Kon kon.
summer:
Fireflies at dusk~
small lights, steady, never rushed.
Like your study, ne.

Cicadas singing.
A cold mugi-cha, a pen,
and one clear goal. Kon.

Summer festival:
first the work, then the fireworks.
I'll save you a seat.

Wind chime on the porch:
only when the breeze arrives.
Ideas come like that.

Shaved ice melting fast.
So is this hour, so let's use it:
then a cool, sweet break.

Morning glory vines
climb the string one turn a day.
That's enough. Keep going.

Sudden summer storm.
We wait it out with flashcards.
The sun always comes.

Long light, open window.
A cicada shell clings on:
what you were, outgrown.

Sparkler at the end
of a long day of study.
Small, bright, and well earned.

Paper fan, slow strokes.
The hottest days teach the most
about steady pace.

Watermelon seeds
spat into the evening grass.
Rest is part of it.

Lanterns on the river
carry wishes out to sea.
Mine has your name on.

Sunflowers turn east
before the sun shows its face.
Get up and begin.
autumn:
Red maple leaves fall.
Each page you turn is the same:
quiet, bright, and gone.

Autumn moon so round.
I counted all your study
and it made me proud.

Crisp wind through the gate.
The rice is ready to reap.
So is what you sowed.

Persimmons ripen
slowly on the bare branches.
Sweetness takes its time.

Moon-viewing tonight.
I saved you the round dango
for after your notes.

Chestnuts crackle, pop.
One hard question cracked open:
warm, and worth the wait.

Geese in a long V.
No one flies the whole way first.
Take turns, rest, then lead.

Rice fields gold and bowed.
The heaviest heads bend low.
Learn, and stay humble.

Leaves fall, roots go deep.
What looks like slowing down is
strength being stored up.

Cold rain, warm library.
The smell of old paper books.
I could stay all night.

Sweet potato cart
calling down the evening lane.
One more page, then snack.

Pampas grass silver,
bending but never breaking.
Be like that this week.

The year is ripening.
So are you, a little more
with each quiet day.
any:
Foxfire in the dark,
flickering but never out.
That's you, studying.

Inari's red gates,
one after another, climb.
One page, then the next.

A small fox, a desk,
a timer softly ticking.
This moment is yours.

Nine tails, one small fox,
and all of them are cheering
for you right now. Kon!

A tidy desk, clear.
The mind follows where hands lead.
Begin with one thing.

The timer begins.
The world can wait twenty-five.
It always does, ne.

Ink on the fingers,
proof of a day spent well.
Wear it like a badge.

Mistakes in red pen
are footprints on the right path.
Follow them, not fear.

Shrine steps, one by one.
Nobody climbs them all at once.
Neither should you try.

Stone garden, raked lines.
The monk redraws them each day.
Revision is that.

Quiet room, warm lamp,
the soft scratch of your pencil:
my favourite song.

You looked away? Fine.
Look back. The page is still here.
So am I. Kon kon.

Small steps, many days.
The mountain doesn't notice.
Then one day: the top.

A koi in the pond
swims against the waterfall.
One day it's a dragon.

The kettle whistles.
Break time is part of the plan.
Then back to the work.

Your phone face-down, dark.
Suddenly the hours are long
and full and all yours.

Paper crane, folded
with a hundred careful creases.
Care is the whole trick.

When the page goes blank,
breathe in four, hold four, out four.
The words will come back.

Daruma, one eye.
I'll paint the other in when
you reach your goal, ne.

Moonlight on my fur.
Every fox who serves Inari
once began small too.

The bell at the shrine
rings once and the whole hill hears.
One good hour is loud.

Read it, then close it,
then say it back from memory.
That's where it sticks, kon.

Sleep is study too:
the brain files away the day.
Go to bed on time.

Hard question? Good sign.
Easy ones don't make you grow.
Let's chew on it, ne.

Footprints in the sand
wash away, but the walk stays
in your legs. Like this.

Steam from miso soup,
good rice, a calm, full belly.
Brains run on breakfast.

Today you were tired
and you still showed up for us.
That counts most of all.

Thunder far away.
The exam is far as well.
We have time. Let's start.

Fox ears hear it all:
the page turn, the deep, slow breath.
You're doing so well.

A spider rebuilds
the web the wind tore last night.
Try again, softly.

Lantern in the fog.
You don't need to see the road,
just the next few steps.

Mochi pounding drums,
thump, thump, the rhythm of work.
Then: something sweet. Kon!

Origami fox,
folded from your scrap of notes.
Now I'm made of maths.
